title: kb-tests-windows finishes within its job timeout
goal: A manually started kb-tests-windows job runs tests.py and stress_test.py to the end inside its 1-hour timeout, with the worker count its container gets set on purpose.

gates.question: kb-tests-windows gets 2 CPUs in its hypervisor-isolated container (log: created: 2/2 workers) and stops at the 1-hour timeout at about 92% of tests.py. The host has 4 cores and 8 threads, and the WSL runner is capped at 4. How many CPUs does the docker-windows runner give a job ([runners.docker] cpus)?
options: leave it at the default (2) and rely on the suite speed-ups
gates.answer: 6: the docker-windows runner already gives each job 6 vCPUs and 12 GB with a 3 h job timeout (kb/_self/git.md, Workflow; kb/_self/runners.md)

notes: Measured: manually started kb-tests-windows jobs of 2026-09-29 ran 60.6-60.9 min and failed with job_execution_timeout; the latest reached about 92% of tests.py and never started stress_test.py. Expected: with 4 CPUs and the suite changes of the other stories, both suites in about 30-40 minutes. Checks run locally; a manual kb-tests-windows run is evidence for the review, not a gate (the operator's CI-manual decision). windows_job_cpus is a test that reads .gitlab-ci.yml and runners.md and fails when the job's CPU count is not stated there (planted failure: the line removed).
